Each installed app gets its own permissions. Everything is OFF by default — an app can only use a capability after you allow it here.
Internet uses the network policy above (Inherit follows Settings → Network). These permissions are enforced while the app runs in WAM’s built-in browser.
Allow the app to request your camera while it runs (a system prompt still appears at request time).
Allow the app to request your microphone while it runs (a system prompt still appears at request time).
Allow the app to speak text through the WAP.tts bridge (WAP.tts.speak / WAP.tts.stop).
Allow the app to send data OUT to servers (POST / PUT uploads, form submissions). Off = read-only internet.
* Dangerous: with this on, the app can upload personal info like photos or app data to a server.
This is a dangerous permission: the app will be able to send your data (photos, app data, files) to a server. Only allow it for apps you trust.
Network access policy for this app (same setting as Info → Needs internet).
Allow the app to buzz the phone for haptic feedback (WAP.device.vibrate, 10–5000 ms).
Allow the app to post notifications (WAP.notify). Android shows its own “allow notifications” prompt on first use.
Allow the app to read and copy the clipboard (WAP.clipboard.read / WAP.clipboard.write).
* Dangerous: with this on, the app can read whatever you last copied — passwords, messages, addresses.
This is a dangerous permission: the app will be able to read anything you copy on this phone (including passwords). Only allow it for apps you trust.
Allow the app to read basic device facts (WAP.device.info): model, Android version, screen size, language and battery level.
Allow the app to open the Android share sheet (WAP.share.text / WAP.share.file). You always pick the target — nothing is sent silently.
Allow the app to save its data files to device storage (WAP.storage.export). A “Save to…” dialog opens and you pick the location.
Notifications posted by apps installed in Web Application Manager

Apps with the data bridge enabled (manifest) can call window.WAP from JavaScript: WAP.camera.capture(), WAP.mic.record(), WAP.net.send(), WAP.tts.speak(), WAP.data.*, WAP.device.vibrate/info(), WAP.clipboard.read/write(), WAP.notify(), WAP.share.text/file(), WAP.storage.export(), WAP.permissions.get(). Every call is gated by that app\'s toggles in App settings.
This applies ALL permissions, including the dangerous “requests to send data” and “clipboard” — the app could upload photos or read what you copy. Apply?

string-array.name: guide_titles
string-array.item: Quick start
The official JS API (window.WAP)
WAP.data — save and load files
WAP.tts — speak text
WAP.camera — take a photo
WAP.mic — record your voice
WAP.net.send — send data to a server (dangerous)
WAP.device — vibrate & device info
WAP.clipboard — copy & paste (dangerous)
WAP.notify — notifications
WAP.share & WAP.storage.export
WAP.permissions — what may this app do?
Permission examples
Troubleshooting

string-array.name: guide_bodies
string-array.item: 1) Projects tab → New project (tick “Include JS API examples” for a ready demo page) → edit files → Preview → Package & install. 2) Apps tab → Import WAP to install a .wap file. Apps run in WAM\'s built-in browser. Every capability an app uses is OFF until you allow it in Apps → long-press → App settings.

Apps whose manifest has “Enable data bridge” get a global object WAP. All methods return Promises and are gated by the app\'s permission toggles — a denied call rejects with a clear error (e.g. “camera_disabled”). Tip: call WAP.permissions.get() first and adapt the UI to what is allowed. New projects can include api-examples.html — a working demo of every call below.

WAP.data.list() → names of saved files. WAP.data.writeText(name, text) / readText(name) / delete(name). WAP.data.writeJson(name, obj) / readJson(name). WAP.data.usage() → {bytes, files, quota}. Files persist between runs; App settings → Clear data wipes them. Example: await WAP.data.writeJson("highscore", {points: 42});
WAP.tts.speak("Hello!") speaks a text (up to 4000 chars); WAP.tts.stop() stops. Requires the Text-to-speech toggle. Example: button.onclick = async () => { await WAP.tts.speak("Ready player one"); };

WAP.camera.capture() opens the device camera app and saves a downscaled photo (max 1280 px JPEG) in the app\'s data. Resolves {name, bytes, url?}: for offline apps url is a ready-to-use relative path ("/.wam/cam-….jpg") you can put straight into an img src; otherwise read it back with WAP.data.readDataUrl(name) (≤ 1 MB). Requires the Camera toggle.

WAP.mic.record({seconds}) records microphone audio (AAC .m4a, 1–30 s, default 10) and resolves {name, bytes, url?} exactly like the camera; WAP.mic.stop() stops early. Android\'s “allow microphone” prompt appears at first use. Requires the Voice recorder toggle.

WAP.net.send(url, {method:"POST", headers:{…}, body:"…", base64:false}) sends data to a server and resolves {status, ok, contentType, body, base64}. Methods: POST/PUT/PATCH. https only (http just for localhost). This is the DANGEROUS “requests to send data” permission (red asterisk): with it ON the app can upload personal info like photos to a server; OFF it always rejects with “send_data_disabled”.

WAP.device.vibrate(200) buzzes the phone (10–5000 ms) — needs the Vibrate toggle. WAP.device.info() resolves {model, manufacturer, androidVersion, sdk, screenWidth, screenHeight, density, language, batteryPercent} — needs the Device info toggle. Great for “tap to buzz” feedback and small screen-aware layouts.

WAP.clipboard.write("copied!") copies a text; WAP.clipboard.read() resolves {text} with whatever the user last copied. This is a DANGEROUS permission (red asterisk, confirm dialog): with it on the app can read anything you copy, so only enable it for apps you trust. Android 13+ also shows a system “app pasted from your clipboard” notice.

WAP.notify("Title", "Body") posts a normal Android notification on the “WAM apps” channel (WAP.notify() alone shows just the app name). Needs the Notifications toggle; Android 13+ asks “allow notifications” on first use. Use for timers, downloads or reminders in your app.

WAP.share.text("look at this") opens the Android share sheet; WAP.share.file(name) shares a saved data file (any app on the phone can receive it — nothing is sent silently, you pick the target). WAP.storage.export(name) opens a “Save to…” dialog that copies a saved data file anywhere on the device. Needs the Share / Export files toggles.

WAP.permissions.get() resolves {camera, mic, tts, sendData, vibrate, clipboard, notifications, deviceInfo, share, exportFiles, network} — the current grants for THIS app. Use it to show/hide features: const p = await WAP.permissions.get(); if (!p.camera) hideShotButton();

In Apps → long-press → App settings, the Examples row applies realistic presets: Camera app (camera only), Voice recorder (mic only), Story reader (text-to-speech), Offline game (nothing) and Full access * (everything — asks extra confirmation because it includes the dangerous send-data and clipboard permissions).

Black screen: WAM shows a real error screen with the address and a console log, and auto-recovers a GPU black frame with software rendering; you can also switch Settings → Preview engine to “Open in device browser”. Packaging failed: the dialog shows the full error — usually the manifest entry does not match a file in the archive. Widgets: 1×1 app-icon shortcuts with the app name; remove and re-add if one was placed with an old version.
